Brute Force Attacks

← Hydra Home

What is Brute Force?

A brute-force attack is a method where every possible password combination is tried until the correct one is found.

Dictionary vs Brute Force

Dictionary attacks use known passwords. Brute force tries every possible combination, making it slower but more complete.

Real Security Use

Ethical hackers simulate brute-force attacks to test how strong authentication systems are under repeated login attempts.

Defenses

Companies prevent these attacks using account lockouts, multi factor authentication, and limiting login attempts per second.
